title: Ready or Not: Korn Ferry Finds One in Four CEO Successions Are Unprepared
summary: Roughly one in four CEO successions lack preparedness according to new research from Korn Ferry.
body_markdown:
**Highlights**


- One in four CEO successions at S&P Global large- and mid-cap companies was unprepared, leaving organizations vulnerable to unexpected leadership transitions.
- Outgoing CEOs in prepared successions served an average of 6.6 years, compared with 3.9 years in unprepared successions.
- Internal candidates filled 75% of CEO roles in prepared successions, compared with 61% in unprepared successions.
- Companies with prepared successions named a successor an average of 15 days after announcing a CEO's departure, compared with 98 days for unprepared successions.


**Los Angeles, November 17, 2026** – Roughly one in four CEO successions lack preparedness according to new research from Korn Ferry (NYSE: KFY). The firm’s analysis of CEO successions across more than 3,600 S&P Global large- and mid-cap companies in 2025 linked insufficient readiness to greater likelihood of abrupt CEO departures, a lack of qualified internal candidates and less time for incoming CEOs to prepare for their role.


As Korn Ferry’s report,[The Readiness Gap](https://www.kornferry.com/institute-articles/the-readiness-gap) , shows, having a CEO succession plan isn't the same as being ready for a CEO transition.


“Most boards have a succession plan, but far fewer could execute a CEO transition tomorrow if they had to,” said Jane Edison Stevenson, Global Vice Chair, Board and CEO Services, and Global Leader, Board and CEO Succession at Korn Ferry. “Strategy cycles are shortening and the CEO mandate is evolving faster than traditional planning can keep pace with. Boards that navigate transitions well treat readiness as an ongoing discipline, not a document they refer to only when a CEO announces a retirement.”


The challenge for boards today has shifted from succession planning to succession readiness.


“Succession readiness cannot be created at the moment of departure,” said Jean-Marc Laouchez, President of the Korn Ferry Institute. “As our research shows, preparedness is built over time through repeated board attention, disciplined HR execution and a leadership mandate that stays tied to strategy. Organizations that do this well preserve their choices, reduce uncertainty and give the next CEO a stronger platform from which to lead.”


Key findings include:


- **Transitions lacking preparation shorten CEO tenures** : In prepared successions, outgoing CEOs served an average of 6.6 years, and only 27% departed within three years. In unprepared successions, average tenure fell to 3.9 years, and 57% left within three years, more than twice the rate in prepared successions.
- **Thoughtful successions produce stronger internal pipelines** : With succession readiness, 75% of CEO roles were filled by internal candidates, compared with 61% in unprepared transitions. While bringing in an external candidate may be the right strategic decision, the risk is being forced into the market because of a lack of readiness among internal successors.
- **Prepared boards identify CEO successors faster** . In prepared successions, boards named a successor an average of 15 days after announcing the outgoing CEO’s departure. In unprepared successions, naming the next CEO took 98 days, more than six times longer.
- **Prepared successors have more time to transition** : Identifying a successor sooner is only half the story. In prepared successions, new leaders had an average of 52 days to prepare for their role, compared to only 14 days in unprepared successions. Having a longer runway allows incoming CEOs to build critical relationships, understand strategic priorities, establish credibility and prepare stakeholders for change.


Despite growing recognition that succession should be continuous, many boards are not consistently reviewing their plans. While 60% of boards in Korn Ferry’s[2026 CEO and Board Survey](https://www.kornferry.com/insights/featured-topics/leadership-articles/ceo-and-board-survey?utm_adtype=always-on&utm_source=google&utm_medium=ppc&utm_campaign=26-08-gbl-ceo-abm-2026&utm_term=korn%20ferry%20board%20recruitment&utm_content=dec&utm_adtype=always-on&utm_adgroup=board-ceo-board-succession-planning&utm_source=google&utm_medium=ppc&utm_campaign=26-01-na-ld-abm&utm_term=korn%20ferry%20board%20recruitment&utm_content=dec&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=22092052200&gclid=EAIaIQobChMI-9eT66OqlgMVYCrUAR1Z4SD3EAAYASABEgInvfD_BwE) said succession should be a continuous process, only 17% review their plans quarterly.


View the full report and methodology[here](https://www.kornferry.com/institute-articles/the-readiness-gap) .
